title: Orchestrated signal-fusion for coordinated canary termination and safe-drain
author: Priya Nair
description:
Motivation: Canary pipelines today make independent decisions from single signals (latency or error-rate). That leads to noisy early terminations or unnecessary holds when signals disagree. This PR introduces a lightweight "signal-fusion" controller that aggregates heterogeneous observability streams (latency percentiles, error budgets, model-quality regressions from evaluation probes, and user-defined quality assertions) and produces a single coordinated decision for canary termination, safe-drain, or rollback.

What this change does (summary):
- Adds a new controller `signal-fusion-orchestrator` that subscribes to existing telemetry feeds and produces a fused decision state for each active rollout.
- Introduces a reconciliation loop with hysteresis and quiesce windows to prevent flip-flopping decisions across upstream metrics blips.
- Adds canary lifecycle hooks: `pre-drain-validation`, `safe-drain-timer`, and `post-terminate-snapshot` so downstream systems (load balancer, cache) can perform graceful shutdown and snapshot telemetry for forensic analysis.
- Exposes a minimal, opt-in rollout config block (`fusionPolicy`) in rollout CRs to tune sensitivity, window sizes, and metric weights. Backwards compatible: if `fusionPolicy` is absent, existing behavior is unchanged.
- Adds unit and integration tests for common failure modes and a synthetic e2e scenario that replays historical incident traces to validate non-flapping behavior.

Behavioral highlights:
- Decision composition: decisions are represented as a three-valued vote per signal (OK, WARN, FAIL) and combined with weighted majority. We treat model-quality regressions (from canary evals) as higher-importance signals than transient 95th percentile latency spikes.
- Hysteresis and backoff: after a FAIL decision, the controller applies a backoff before allowing a new promote decision. After WARN, the controller will extend canary hold windows rather than immediately rollback.
- Safe-drain: when a final terminate decision is issued, the safe-drain timer triggers a drain window (configurable, default 60s) and emits a `pre-drain-validation` event allowing LB/caching layers to quiesce. On expiration, `post-terminate-snapshot` stores aggregated telemetry into the rollout journal for replay.
- Rollback automation: the controller can optionally attach an automatic rollback action (disabled by default). When enabled and policy threshold is breached, the controller initiates a transactional swap to the previous pinned model and records a rollback reason using the same telemetry snapshot.

Configuration example (rollout snippet):
```
rollout:
  id: rollout-2026-02-pri
  modelVersion: v2.7.3
  fusionPolicy:
    enabled: true
    metricWeights:
      latency_p95: 0.2
      error_rate: 0.3
      eval_regression: 0.4
      user_assertions: 0.1
    windows:
      evaluationWindowSeconds: 120
      holdWindowSeconds: 300
      safeDrainSeconds: 60
    hysteresis:
      failCooldownSeconds: 900
      warnExtendFactor: 2.0
    autoRollback: false
```

Checklist (this PR):
- [x] Controller implementation and reconciliation loop
- [x] Rollout API extension and validation schema
- [x] Unit tests for voting logic and hysteresis
- [x] Integration test that runs synthetic telemetry replay
- [x] E2E replay harness using incident traces (local)
- [x] Docs: rollout reference and migration note (docs/rollouts/signal-fusion.md)

Testing & validation:
- Added `TestVoteAggregation` and `TestHysteresisBackoff` unit tests.
- Integration test `FusionReplayIntegration` replays a small historical incident trace (from infra/telemetry/testdata/incident-2025-11.json) and asserts no-flapping across three successive short blips.
- Perf: controller CPU < 40m on a 2vCPU pod at 1k rollout/sec fanout (bench harness in perf/).

Migration notes: Existing rollout definitions without `fusionPolicy` operate unchanged. Admins who enable `fusionPolicy` should start with conservative weights and larger windows to avoid overreaction.

Why this is unique/different from previous rollout work: Prior work focused on traffic-phasing, cohort routing and shadow validation. This PR centralizes decisioning across signals and lifecycle hooks to simplify safe termination and post-mortem telemetry collection. It is intentionally opt-in and targeted at teams running multi-signal canaries (latency+quality).

Related linear items: ENG-5421 (signal-fusion controller), PM-881 (rollout UX), ENG-5512 (canary journaling). More details in docs/rollouts/signal-fusion.md.
